assumptions: #1298: an untimestamped v1 entry's run_id is `<suite>-<commit>-0-<sha256(canonical entry)[:12]>`. Two byte-identical untimestamped entries for one commit are treated as one run: the second is reported skipped. That matches the existing rule for two timestamped entries in the same second.

#1298: `Migrated N` counts writes. Ids already in the store are read through the optional AsyncHistoryStore.readAll (local NDJSON). The remote Supabase backend has no readAll and upserts, so a re-push there does write and is counted.
#1298: readAll now runs before the loop, so a store with corrupt or unsupported content aborts migrate, dry-run included. Before this change, the first pushRun hit the same read and threw anyway.
#1298: untimestamped entries migrated by an earlier version carry clock-based ids, so re-migrating them adds them again under the new ids. The CHANGELOG notes this.
#1350: a test's flake identity is (test_file, test_name). Rows written before #1021, or rows with no file, can split one test into two tallies. No path normalisation is applied on read.
#1350: ci-ready's reason keeps the bare test name and adds ` (<file>)` only when two files in the window share that name.
#1350: the remote Supabase `canary_flake_summary` view is defined outside this repository and is unchanged.
#1350 (F2 = a): ndjson-store.ts was paid down from 299 to 277 lines in a separate pure-refactor commit before the fix. No allowance or baseline file was edited.
